### Introduction:

This time you will create the data.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
```

### Step 2. Create a data list

```{r given-data}
raw_data <- list(
  name = c("Bulbasaur", "Charmander", "Squirtle", "Caterpie"),
  evolution = c("Ivysaur", "Charmeleon", "Wartortle", "Metapod"),
  type = c("grass", "fire", "water", "bug"),
  hp = c(45, 39, 44, 45),
  pokedex = c("yes", "no", "yes", "no")
)
```

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called pokemon

```{r}
pokemon <- as_tibble(raw_data)
head(pokemon)
```

### Step 4. Place the order of the columns as name, type, hp, evolution, pokedex

```{r}
# (old versions of pandas sorted the columns alphabetically; R keeps the order of the list)
pokemon <- pokemon |> select(name, type, hp, evolution, pokedex)
pokemon
```

### Step 5. Add another column called place, and insert what you have in mind.

```{r}
pokemon <- pokemon |> mutate(place = c("park", "street", "lake", "forest"))
pokemon
```

### Step 6. Present the type of each column

```{r}
sapply(pokemon, class)

# or
glimpse(pokemon)
```
